findings.summary: openMenu() adds `document.addEventListener('click', onClickOutside)` but closeMenu() only removes the keydown listener — it never calls `document.removeEventListener('click', onClickOutside)`. This is the exact behavior the brief explicitly required ('cleaning up any listeners added for the outside-click detection once the menu is closed, so they don't keep firing after the menu is dismissed'). Concretely: once the menu has been opened and closed once, onClickOutside stays bound to document forever. Every subsequent click anywhere on the page (menu closed) re-enters onClickOutside, which finds neither menuEl nor toggleEl contains the click target and calls closeMenu() again — which calls `toggleEl.focus()`, silently stealing keyboard focus to the hamburger button on every click on the page from then on. This is a real, user-visible regression, not just a lingering no-op listener.
